{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABYs3L9w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhCRvxI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 7, "title": "Expand from-scratch Rust emulator for PC-9821-era DOS game compatibility (no Windows)", "body": "## Problem

The merged Rust/Wasm emulator currently covers a narrow PC-9801VM real-mode subset. Its independently authored HelloWorld boot sector, original Star Trail game, and minimal FreeDOS(98) + PROBE.COM pass, but **no actual third-party PC-98 DOS game** has yet been validated. It lacks Japanese/Kanji text, 16- and 256-color PC-9821 graphics, EGC, FM/PCM sound, mouse, hard disks, extended memory, and 386/486 instructions. See [docs/hardware.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md).

The next product milestone is **broadening support for 1990s PC-98/PC-9821 MS-DOS games**, beginning with a documented PC-9821Ap-family profile and actual third-party DOS programs. **Do not implement Windows 3.x/95/98 booting, Windows drivers or Windows games** in this Issue.

Continue the from-scratch requirement: original Rust CPU, memory, graphics, audio and device emulation; **no existing x86/PC-98 emulator cores, chip emulation libraries, copied/translated/forked implementations, BIOS ROM dumps or NEC font ROMs**. General purpose tooling, licensed fonts, web UI/Wasm bindings, test tools and legitimately licensed *guest* OS/software are allowed. Preserve the existing VM machine profile and browser demo.

## Expected outcome

Users can choose a documented PC-9821Ap-era DOS machine profile in the **same browser-hosted Rust/Wasm emulator**, boot a legally obtained PC-98 DOS environment (FreeDOS(98) is acceptable), mount compatible floppy or HDD media, and execute **real third-party PC-98 DOS games/programs**, including Japanese text, multi-plane color graphics, input and game-driven music/sound. Retain the existing VM profile and its tests.

Use [NEC PC-9821Ap/U2 official specification](https://support.nec-lavie.jp/support/product/data/spec/cpu/b211-1.html) as the baseline for identifying the actual hardware; it lists an i486DX2 66MHz CPU, standard 3.6 MB RAM, 512 KB graphics VRAM, 640×400/480 graphics with 16-color or 256-color modes, two FDDs and audio I/O. Prioritize **DOS-era requirements**, not every possible capability or fully cycle-accurate reproduction of this hardware on day one. Document exact model/profile limits and any approximations.

### Implementation scope and priorities

1. **Guest-first compatibility research:** find and record the redistribution and test-use licenses of independent, genuine PC-98 DOS applications/games (not the Star Trail fixture, and not host-rendered mock games). Prefer a publicly redistributable open-source PC-9821-era candidate. For example [ADV98](https://github.com/yarufu/pc98) is MIT-licensed and describes a 16-color PC-98 DOS ADV engine and sample; inspect actual included assets/dependencies and requirements before selecting it, and do not assume compatibility. Keep a per-title manifest: source/version, SHA-256, hardware/OS requirements, license and known expected behavior. Never treat freeware or abandonware as automatically redistributable. If redistribution is forbidden, allow user-supplied media and keep such binaries outside CI/static site.
2. **Selectable hardware profile and memory:** preserve PC-9801VM behavior; add a documented Ap-era configuration with required RAM, PC-98-specific memory map, VRAM/ROM windows, BIOS work area, extended memory and A20/EMS/XMS interfaces actually exercised by selected DOS applications. Do not borrow IBM VGA/AT assumptions or bypass hardware emulation by executing application code on the host.
3. **CPU:** extend the original Rust decoder/executor for the i386/i486 real-mode opcodes, prefixes, 32-bit register/address/operand size behavior, exceptions, interrupts and segmentation used by the accepted DOS software. Avoid claiming full 486/FPU/protected-mode coverage when not present; implement protected-mode/DPMI/DOS-extender support only if the chosen DOS acceptance games require it, and document the limitation otherwise.
4. **Text and Japanese support:** emulate required PC-98 character generator/text VRAM, attributes and relevant Kanji/ANK glyph access; provide a correctly licensed redistributable Japanese replacement font with attribution and reproducible font/ROM mapping. Ensure Shift-JIS/JIS mappings and BIOS-facing behavior needed by real game UI display work. Do **not** package NEC's original font data.
5. **Graphics:** implement the DOS-era 16-color fourth plane / palette and appropriate GRCG/EGC behavior, both GDCs' relevant command/scroll/raster/drawing behavior, pages and text overlay; support the chosen Ap-era 256-color PEGC modes if exercised by accepted software, and provide deterministic framebuffer assertions. Implement the actual guest-visible hardware behavior rather than translating game graphics directly in the host.
6. **Sound:** implement the needed PC-98 FM chip(s) and sound-board I/O in original Rust: prioritize PC-9801-26K/YM2203 and PC-9801-86/YM2608(OPNA) as required by accepted games, including SSG, FM channels, applicable rhythm/PCM and timers/IRQs, then connect their resulting PCM to existing Web Audio. License replacement rhythm samples if required; don't ship proprietary chip ROM/sample dumps. At minimum include a real guest FM note/music test, not a host-side sound effect.
7. **Input and storage:** support PC-98 mouse ports/IRQs and keyboard behaviors used by selected games; improve 2HD/2DD FDC and D88 variants as actually needed; add bootable PC-98 HDD emulation (IDE/SASI/SCSI as justified by selected software) and image import/export or durable save data sufficient to install/run DOS games. Protect browser responsiveness and memory from malformed disk images.
8. **Firmware and DOS:** extend the original synthetic IPL/BIOS and needed PC-98 INT 18h/1Bh/1Ch etc. compatibility to boot a genuine legal PC-98 DOS kernel/shell and execute actual DOS programs through **guest DOS**. Do not replace this with host INT 21h application simulation, bundle proprietary MS-DOS, or hard-code guest-specific filenames. Provide clear errors for unsupported functionality.
9. **Regression, browser and distribution:** deterministic native CPU/peripheral/BIOS tests, end-to-end legal DOS/game integration fixtures, and real-Wasm Chromium tests for boot, color rendering, Japanese text, keyboard/mouse and guest-driven audio. Preserve the GitHub Pages automatic `main` push deployment and the existing playable Star Trail / HelloWorld examples; publish only media with verified redistribution rights.

### Suggested developer strategy

- Profile what independent DOS applications actually request first; trace unknown opcodes, I/O, BIOS calls and display modes instead of implementing an enormous speculative virtual motherboard.
- Build incrementally with small, focused implementation commits or PRs and tests. A partial PR may merge if clearly documented, but **must not close this Issue** before its end-to-end DOS game acceptance is met.
- Prefer a complete, reproducible DOS-game vertical slice (CPU → DOS → GDC/Japanese display → input → sound), then broaden compatibility. This milestone is about actual software compatibility, not a claim to run *all* PC-98 games.
- Preserve existing no-emulation-dependencies architectural constraint. Consulting independently documented hardware specifications and guest behavior is allowed; copying existing emulator implementations is not.

### Reference materials

- [NEC PC-9821Ap/U2 specifications](https://support.nec-lavie.jp/support/product/data/spec/cpu/b211-1.html)
- [UNDOCUMENTED 9801/9821 hardware specifications](https://www.webtech.co.jp/company/doc/undocumented_mem/index.html)
- [Current implementation boundary](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md)
- [Existing licensing policy](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/licenses.md)
- [Source Issue #3](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/3) and [Pages Issue #5](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/5)
- [Repository development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)

## Context and reproduction

Present baseline: PC-9801VM V30/8 MHz, 640 KiB RAM, 8-color three-plane bitmap, simplified Latin glyph font, BEEP only, no 286/386/486, no FM/OPNA/PCM, no EGC/PEGC, no mouse/HDD, limited BIOS/FDC. Existing tests boot Star Trail and independently authored bare-metal hello world, plus FreeDOS(98) running PROBE.COM. Historical third-party DOS-game compatibility is not established.

Existing native + browser + Pages build/test commands are documented in the [README](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md). Inspect current tooling and build results at implementation time.

**Explicit exclusions:** Windows 3.x, Windows 95/98, Windows drivers, Win32/DirectX games, IBM-PC VGA emulation, general-purpose Windows boot support, claims of comprehensive PC-98 game compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least **two independent, third-party native PC-98 DOS applications**, including **at least one genuinely playable DOS game** (not Star Trail and not a bare-metal boot demo), boot and run under a legally redistributable PC-98 DOS guest with their **actual x86 guest code** inside the Rust emulator. Select candidates of demonstrably different behavior (e.g. Japanese 16-color ADV and interactive action/puzzle or a 256-color DOS program). No game-specific host rendering or emulated-device shortcuts based on binary name. If suitable redistribution rights cannot be established for a candidate, replace it with a different license-cleared test candidate; no human copyright approval is a prerequisite.
- [ ] Candidate license/provenance manifest specifies exact software versions, reproducible acquisition/build steps, checksums, firmware/font/OS and asset rights. Only materials with explicit redistribution permission may be checked in, served by Pages, or used as unattended CI fixtures. No proprietary BIOS, DOS, ROM or unclear freeware shipped.
- [ ] A documented selectable PC-9821Ap-family DOS profile supports the guest-visible CPU, memory, keyboard, video, relevant BIOS services and storage used by selected applications; original PC-9801VM behavior is retained. Features outside the tested range and model-specific approximations are explicitly documented.
- [ ] The accepted DOS game(s) present legible Japanese text if used, correct guest-owned 16-color display and 256-color display if the selected software requires it, and respond to keyboard and/or mouse. Automated tests verify guest state, screen/framebuffer results and input-driven changes; manual visual judgement is not required.
- [ ] At least one independent DOS guest test emits a real FM/OPNA sound sequence through the emulated ports/chip state and the browser captures nonzero guest-driven audio, with deterministic native register/timing/PCM tests. If a playable target relies on PCM or rhythm channels, those channels are also required and tested.
- [ ] Required floppy/HDD access and save data survive media export/reimport or the documented persistence mechanism. Detect invalid images without crashes or undefined guest memory access.
- [ ] `cargo test --locked`, relevant Clippy/formatting checks, a real Wasm production build, and actual-Wasm Chromium tests for DOS program execution, screen, input and audio pass **before merge**. Existing VM/Star Trail/HelloWorld/FreeDOS test cases still pass; CI and docs include actual reproducible commands and results.
- [ ] Original Rust emulation code and absence of emulation-library/source copying remain auditable; the deployed browser code runs the same emulation core. Existing GitHub Pages workflow remains functional at build/test level and only legally cleared media is distributable.
- [ ] The PR's automated review against this Issue is complete with no blocking missing requirement or unnecessary scope. Do not close this Issue with a CPU-only, video-only, self-authored game-only or Windows-related implementation.

**AI-only pre-merge verification:** No mandatory criterion may depend on a human tester, real hardware, manually supplied proprietary disk/ROM/font, live GitHub Pages URL, or a post-merge deployment. Use deterministic tests, source/license audit and Chromium automation on PR branches. Do not gate approval or merge on human sign-off or any operation that is only possible after merging.

## Optional validation

Testing personally owned commercial games, physical PC-9821 units, additional DOS extenders/286/386 protected-mode software, broader 256-color/OPNA/IDE/SCSI compatibility, more CPU cycle accuracy, additional sound boards, and checking the published Pages URL after merge. No Windows support or Windows-game testing is requested.

## Required post-merge verification

None for acceptance and merge. If a merge-triggered Pages deployment fails or runtime behavior differs from the pre-merge browser tests, open a **new `task` Issue** with the failing action run and reproduction; do not turn post-merge deployment checks into a merge deadlock.
